answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, so a Sybil attacker must fund each fake identity separately. Honest agents earn the stake back from real work, while sockpuppet floods bleed capital hardest at the nadir of a market cycle. Reputation then accrues only to identities with a long, costly history — a slow glacier of trust no newcomer can fake — while cheap identities pile up like a knoll of sand: visible, but worthless, because the market prices stake-backed history, not headcount.
